open_weights.note: This record describes Perplexity's proprietary hosted Sonar service, not a downloadable checkpoint. An upstream open-weight model would not make the service itself open weights.

license.note: Descriptive classification for the hosted model under Perplexity API terms. No MIT license is inherited from an asserted R1 ancestor.

parameters_b.note: Nominal historical language-backbone total inferred from explicit developer lineage: Perplexity’s April 5, 2025 archived model overview identifies sonar-reasoning-pro as powered by DeepSeek R1; DeepSeek publishes 671B total for R1. Reviewed later exact-model and research material discloses no pruning, distillation, expert expansion or replacement that defeats this inference. The exact fine-tuned checkpoint and later service backend remain unspecified, but an exact tensor census is not required to retain this supported nominal specification. Accept with proposed language_backbone scope; do not interpret it as all hosted-service components.

active_parameters_b.note: Nominal 37B activated parameters per token for the historically identified DeepSeek-R1 language backbone, supported separately by DeepSeek’s total/activated table and Perplexity’s deployment article. This is not inferred by equating active with total. The exact served checkpoint, batch-wide union of activated experts, speculative draft and auxiliary retrieval/vision components are outside this per-token backbone figure. Accept with proposed language_backbone scope.

architecture.note: Historical language-backbone architecture inferred from Perplexity’s explicit DeepSeek R1 identification. DeepSeek’s model card identifies R1 as MoE, corroborated by Perplexity’s deployment research. This does not specify auxiliary image-processing components, an exact fine-tuned checkpoint, or a later Agent API backend.

context_window.note: Last documented 128K; distributor corroborates decimal 128000. Earlier reproduced docs show 127K. Retain the later legacy limit, without asserting current backend behavior.

modalities.note: Retain documented API-level text/image input and text output. Exact card specifically restricts image input combined with structured outputs, consistent with the legacy media guide and distributor metadata. Does not establish a natively multimodal backbone or image generation.

reasoning.note: Explicit Chain-of-Thought capability; exact response example includes a thinking section.

tool_call.note: Clear blanket false. Retrieval and citations are established, but reviewed exact-model evidence does not establish model-selected tool invocation or custom function calling. November Pro Search tool orchestration is explicitly Sonar Pro; it is not borrowed. Conflicting distributor tool flags do not resolve the issue.

patch.notes: Release month: February 2025. The original publisher model table has no Reasoning Pro on January 30 and adds it by February 5; a January 31 native discussion reproduces the pre-Pro list. NanoGPT announces the new Pro release on February 3, and a February 4 native API discussion reports its new deployment. This combined chronology supports the month; the exact first day is not established. The January 28/29 sibling launch, February 5 archive capture and March 7 OpenRouter listing are not used as the release day. The 128K context and image-input restrictions describe the legacy service. Sonar Chat Completions support ended September 27, 2026; compatibility requests are gradually reformulated through Agent API, so successful requests do not verify the original backend. Fresh October 27 parameter re-audit recovered an April 5, 2025 archive of Perplexity’s own model overview explicitly identifying sonar-reasoning-pro as powered by DeepSeek R1. DeepSeek’s official card and Perplexity’s deployment research establish the nominal R1 specifications of 671B total, 37B activated per token and MoE architecture. Retain those as a documented lineage inference for the historical language backbone, together with the proposed component and active scopes; no reviewed primary source discloses structural changes defeating the inference. Exact fine-tuned checkpoint, later backend revisions and auxiliary search, routing, image-processing or speculative-decoding components remain unspecified and are not counted. Missing exact deployed tensor sizes do not invalidate the nominal backbone specification. Tool invocation remains unverified; built-in retrieval alone does not establish model-selected tools, and Sonar Pro’s Pro Search capabilities are not inherited.

summary: Fresh October 27 parameter re-audit recovered archived first-party documentation explicitly tying Sonar Reasoning Pro to DeepSeek R1. Restore nominal 671B total and 37B activated per token, with MoE architecture, as historical language-backbone specifications inferred from that developer binding and the official R1 card. Accept these values with the proposed component and active scopes. The exact fine-tuned checkpoint, auxiliary components and later backend remain unspecified; model-selected tool support remains unresolved. Other audited fields are preserved. October 28 release-date review resolves the month to February 2025 from original before/after publisher tables and contemporaneous native launch observations; no exact day is asserted. All thirteen other field assessments, parameter evidence/scopes and earlier research metadata are preserved.
